title: False claims about miscarriage risk from Covid-19 vaccines are spreading online. They use a faulty interpretation of data
facts: US Senators Ron Johnson and Rand Paul released text messages retrieved from Dr. Anthony Fauci's former government phone.
Misleading online claims asserted an 82% miscarriage risk associated with Covid-19 vaccines.
Dr. Kevin Ault serves as an ob/gyn and president-elect of the National Foundation for Infectious Diseases.
A vaccine registry study published in the New England Journal of Medicine in April 2021 tracked nearly 4,000 vaccinated women.
The April 2021 study identified 827 completed pregnancies, which included 712 live births and 104 spontaneous abortions.
The average natural miscarriage rate in the general population ranges from 10% to 20% according to the Mayo Clinic.
The New England Journal of Medicine issued a formal correction to the pregnancy vaccine study in September 2021.
Seven hundred of the completed pregnancies in the 2021 vaccine study involved vaccination during the third trimester.
The inaccurate 82% miscarriage figure was calculated by excluding 700 third-trimester pregnancies from the denominator.
Dr. Brenna Hughes chairs the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine's Infectious Disease and Emerging Threats Committee.
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed that Covid-19 vaccination does not increase health risks during pregnancy.
Studies demonstrate that Covid-19 vaccination during pregnancy provides protective antibodies to both mother and infant.
Dr. Anthony Fauci discussed Covid-19 vaccine safety in pregnancy in text messages from January 2021.
Medical researchers documented hundreds of maternal deaths caused by Covid-19 infections during 2021.
Covid-19 infection during pregnancy increases the risk of intensive care admissions, preterm delivery, and stillbirth.
